key_insight: A D-gun sprayed Al2O3-TiO2 coating substantially improves the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and the wear response can be predicted effectively with machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This supports using hard ceramic coatings plus data-driven wear prediction to extend component life in aerospace, biomedical, and marine Ti-6Al-4V applications.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 coating to Ti-6Al-4V by detonation gun spraying.
Tested wear using ASTM G99 pin-on-disc trials against EN31 steel under 40–100 N, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min.
Built ANN, KNN, and random forest models to predict wear from sliding parameters.
evidence_signal: SEM showed a protective tribo-layer on coated samples, and random forest achieved the lowest prediction error among the evaluated models.
watch_item: The predictive models are based on a limited test range and material system, so broader validation is needed before use outside the tested loading and speed conditions.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
